## Documentation Index
While building apps on the developer platform, you can configure authentication based on how you plan to install your app. HubSpot also provides local authentication tooling via the HubSpot CLI.

## [​](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/developer-platform/build-apps/authentication/overview#app-authentication)  App authentication
### [​](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/developer-platform/build-apps/authentication/overview#oauth)  OAuth
```
curl --request GET \
--header "Authorization: Bearer 00000000-aaaa-xxx-yyyy-zzzzzzzzzzzz" \
--url "https://api.hubapi.com/crm/objects/2026-03/contacts?limit=10&archived=false"
```

### [​](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/developer-platform/build-apps/authentication/overview#static-auth)  Static auth
```
curl --request GET \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ***-***-*********-****-****-****-************" \
--url "https://api.hubapi.com/crm/objects/2026-03/contacts?limit=10&archived=false"
```

## [​](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/developer-platform/build-apps/authentication/overview#developer-api-keys)  Developer API keys
Some app features and settings require a developer API key, which is available in the developer overview of your HubSpot account.If a feature or endpoint requires a developer API key, it’ll be documented in the associated guide or reference article.

name: Help Scout
one_liner:
# Overview
## Authentication [Anchor link for: authentication](https://developer.helpscout.com/docs-api/#authentication)
This is an HTTPS-only API. Authentication is based on API keys. Each API key is associated with a Help Scout user. Results returned from various responses are based upon the role of the user to which the API key is tied.

The API key is passed via HTTP Basic Authentication and goes in the username field. A dummy password, such as X, goes in the password field.

To try the API via curl on the command-line, the general form used would be:

```html
curl --user API_KEY:DUMMY_PASSWORD API_URL
```

For instance, if your API key is 60783dd23ef, you would execute:

```html
curl --user 60783dd23ef:X https://docsapi.helpscout.net/v1/collections
```

```xml
Status: 404 Not Found
{
    "code": 404,
    "error": "Resource not found"
}
```

### Authentication[authentication](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/rest/#authentication)
Adobe Commerce REST APIs support multiple [authentication methods](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/get-started/authentication/), including:

- Third-party applications authenticate with [OAuth 1.0a](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/get-started/authentication/gs-authentication-oauth).
- Mobile applications authenticate using [tokens](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/get-started/authentication/gs-authentication-token).
- Administrators and customers are authenticated with [login credentials](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/get-started/authentication/gs-authentication-token).

## Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service[adobe-commerce-as-a-cloud-service](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/rest/#adobe-commerce-as-a-cloud-service)
### Authentication[authentication-1](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/rest/#authentication-1)
In previous versions of Adobe Commerce, you would use authentication tokens to authorize your requests to the REST API. In Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service, you must use Adobe Identity Management Service (IMS) to [authenticate your requests](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/rest/authentication/).

The authentication system supports both [interactive user-based workflows](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/rest/authentication/user) and automated [server-to-server integrations](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/rest/authentication/server-to-server), ensuring secure and appropriate access for different use cases. Both of these authentication methods require every request to be signed with an IMS Access Token.

[Section titled “Authentication”](https://docs.netlify.com/api-and-cli-guides/api-guides/get-started-with-api/#authentication)

Netlify uses OAuth2 for authentication. All requests must use HTTPS.

To generate a personal access token (PAT):

Use your PAT for manual authentication in shell scripts or commands that use the Netlify API.

To authenticate API requests, include the token in the authorization header:

`Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN>`

This allows users to authorize your application to use Netlify on their behalf without having to copy/paste API tokens or touch sensitive login info. You’ll need an application client key and a client secret to integrate with the Netlify API. You can register a new application in your Netlify user settings for [OAuth applications](https://app.netlify.com/applications).
